articles.title: HumanaChoice H5216-347 PPO - Plan Overview
articles.summary: HumanaChoice H5216-347 PPO is a Medicare Advantage Preferred Provider Organization plan offering nationwide coverage with no referral requirements for specialists. Members benefit from significantly lower costs when using in-network providers.

sections.title: Plan Overview
sections.content: HumanaChoice H5216-347 PPO is a Medicare Advantage Preferred Provider Organization plan offering nationwide coverage. Members may see any Medicare-approved provider. Using Humana's in-network providers results in significantly lower copays and coinsurance. No referral is required for specialists.

sections.title: Plan Type and Network
sections.content: This is a Preferred Provider Organization (PPO) plan which means you have flexibility to see any Medicare-approved provider nationwide. You'll save money by using Humana's in-network providers. You don't need referrals to see specialists.

articles.title: Cost Structure and Deductibles
articles.summary: Detailed breakdown of annual deductibles, out-of-pocket maximums, and cost-sharing structure for in-network and out-of-network services.

sections.title: Annual Deductible
sections.content: The annual deductible is the amount you pay for covered healthcare services before your insurance plan starts to pay. In-network deductible is $325. Out-of-network deductible is $850.

sections.title: Annual Out-of-Pocket Maximum
sections.content: The out-of-pocket maximum is the most you'll pay for covered services in a year. Once you reach this amount, your insurance pays 100% of covered services. In-network maximum is $4,500. Combined in-network and out-of-network maximum is $8,000.

articles.title: Medical Services Coverage
articles.summary: Comprehensive coverage details for medical services including primary care, specialist visits, urgent care, emergency room, and hospital stays.

sections.title: Primary Care Visits
sections.content: Primary care visits include appointments with your primary care physician for routine checkups, preventive care, and treatment of common illnesses.

sections.title: Specialist Visits
sections.content: Specialist visits are appointments with doctors who specialize in specific areas of medicine. No referral is required to see a specialist with this PPO plan.

sections.title: Urgent Care
sections.content: Urgent care facilities provide treatment for non-life-threatening medical conditions that require immediate attention but are not severe enough for the emergency room.

sections.title: Emergency Room
sections.content: Emergency room services are for life-threatening or severe medical conditions requiring immediate medical attention. The copay is the same whether you go to an in-network or out-of-network emergency room. The copay is waived if you are admitted to the hospital.

sections.title: Inpatient Hospital Stay
sections.content: Inpatient hospital stays are when you are formally admitted to a hospital for medical treatment or surgery that requires an overnight stay.

sections.title: Outpatient Surgery
sections.content: Outpatient surgery includes surgical procedures that don't require an overnight hospital stay. You can go home the same day after the procedure.

articles.title: Diagnostic Services and Imaging
articles.summary: Coverage information for diagnostic laboratory tests and imaging services including MRI, CT scans, and PET scans.

sections.title: Diagnostic Labs
sections.content: Diagnostic laboratory tests include blood work, urinalysis, and other lab tests ordered by your doctor to diagnose or monitor health conditions.

sections.title: Imaging Services
sections.content: Imaging services include advanced diagnostic imaging such as MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging), CT (Computed Tomography) scans, and PET (Positron Emission Tomography) scans.

articles.title: Telehealth and Virtual Care
articles.summary: Information about telehealth services allowing virtual visits with primary care physicians and specialists.

sections.title: Telehealth Services
sections.content: Telehealth allows you to have virtual appointments with healthcare providers using video or phone. This is convenient for non-emergency medical issues and follow-up visits.

articles.title: Ambulance Services
articles.summary: Coverage for emergency ambulance services for both in-network and out-of-network providers.

sections.title: Ambulance Services
sections.content: Ambulance services include emergency medical transportation by ground or air ambulance when medically necessary.

cost_details.note: Same cost for both in-network and out-of-network

articles.title: Prescription Drug Coverage (Part D)
articles.summary: Comprehensive prescription drug coverage with a three-tier formulary covering preferred generics, non-preferred generics, preferred brand drugs, and specialty medications.

sections.title: Prescription Drug Overview
sections.content: The plan uses a three-tier formulary for prescription drug coverage. Different tiers have different copays. You can get prescriptions at retail pharmacies for 30-day supplies or use mail-order for 90-day supplies at lower costs.

sections.title: Tier 1 - Preferred Generics
sections.content: Tier 1 includes preferred generic medications which are the most affordable option. These are generic drugs that are on Humana's preferred list.

sections.title: Tier 2 - Non-Preferred Generics
sections.content: Tier 2 includes non-preferred generic medications. These are still generic drugs but not on Humana's preferred list, so they cost slightly more than Tier 1.

sections.title: Tier 3 - Preferred Brand Drugs
sections.content: Tier 3 includes preferred brand-name medications. These are brand-name drugs that are on Humana's preferred list.

sections.title: Tier 4 - Specialty Drugs
sections.content: Tier 4 includes specialty medications which are high-cost drugs that treat complex conditions. These must be filled through a specialty pharmacy and are limited to 30-day supplies.

cost_details.requirement: Must be filled through specialty pharmacy

sections.title: Specialty Medication Rules
sections.content: Specialty medications have special requirements. Prior authorization is required for all specialty drugs. Any specialty drug costing more than $2,000 requires enrollment in Humana's specialty case-management program.

articles.title: Preventive Care
articles.summary: Comprehensive preventive care services covered at 100% in-network with no deductible, copay, or coinsurance including annual physicals, screenings, and vaccinations.

sections.title: Preventive Care Overview
sections.content: The plan covers preventive services at 100% in-network with no deductible, no copay, and no coinsurance. Out-of-network preventive care typically requires 40% coinsurance.

sections.title: Covered Preventive Services
sections.content: Preventive services include annual physical examinations, mammograms, pap smears, colonoscopy once every 10 years, flu vaccines, COVID-19 vaccines, Hepatitis B vaccinations, diabetes screenings, and cardiovascular risk assessments.

articles.title: Mental Health and Substance Use Coverage
articles.summary: Coverage for mental health services including outpatient therapy, psychiatrist visits, inpatient mental health treatment, and substance use disorder treatment.

sections.title: Outpatient Mental Health Therapy
sections.content: Outpatient mental health therapy includes visits with therapists, counselors, psychologists, or social workers for mental health treatment.

sections.title: Psychiatrist Visits
sections.content: Psychiatrist visits include appointments with medical doctors who specialize in mental health and can prescribe medications.

sections.title: Inpatient Mental Health
sections.content: Inpatient mental health treatment includes hospitalization for mental health conditions requiring intensive treatment and 24-hour care.

sections.title: Substance Use Disorder Treatment
sections.content: Substance use disorder treatment includes services for alcohol and drug addiction including outpatient counseling and inpatient rehabilitation programs.

cost_details.inpatient: Same structure as mental health inpatient (Days 1-5: $295/day, Days 6+: $0)

articles.title: Additional Benefits
articles.summary: Additional benefits beyond medical coverage including vision care, dental services, hearing aids, and fitness programs.

sections.title: Vision Benefit
sections.content: Vision benefits include routine eye exams and an allowance for glasses or contact lenses each year.

sections.title: Dental Benefit
sections.content: Dental benefits include preventive services like cleanings and exams at no cost, basic restorative dental with cost-sharing, but major procedures are not covered.

sections.title: Hearing Benefit
sections.content: Hearing benefits include routine hearing exams at no cost and discounted hearing aids through the Humana TruHearing program.

sections.title: Fitness Benefit
sections.content: Fitness benefit includes the SilverSneakers program at no extra cost, providing access to fitness centers and exercise classes.

articles.title: Prior Authorization Requirements
articles.summary: Services and procedures that require prior authorization from Humana before receiving care to ensure coverage.

sections.title: Prior Authorization Overview
sections.content: Certain services require prior authorization from Humana before you receive care. Failure to obtain authorization may cause claim denials, meaning you could be responsible for the full cost of the service.

sections.title: Services Requiring Prior Authorization
sections.content: The following services require prior authorization: MRI, CT, and PET imaging; any inpatient hospital admission; outpatient surgeries that cost more than $2,000; home health care services; durable medical equipment (DME) costing more than $500; all specialty prescriptions; skilled nursing facility admissions; and hospice services (notification only).
services_requiring_authorization: Durable Medical Equipment (DME) costing more than $500

articles.title: Exclusions and Non-Covered Services
articles.summary: Services and treatments that are not covered by the HumanaChoice H5216-347 PPO plan.

sections.title: Non-Covered Services
sections.content: HumanaChoice H5216-347 PPO does not cover the following services: cosmetic surgery unless medically necessary; long-term custodial care; routine foot care (not related to diabetes); experimental or investigational treatments; non-emergency services outside the U.S.; elective dental procedures such as implants or orthodontics; personal convenience items in hospital rooms; and acupuncture (unless for chronic low back pain as defined by Medicare guidelines).
non_covered_services: Routine foot care (not related to diabetes)
Personal convenience items in hospital rooms
Acupuncture (except for chronic low back pain per Medicare guidelines)

common_queries.query: What is the deductible for this plan?
common_queries.answer: The annual deductible is $325 for in-network services and $850 for out-of-network services.
The out-of-pocket maximum is $4,500 for in-network services. The combined in-network and out-of-network maximum is $8,000.

common_queries.query: Do I need a referral to see a specialist?
common_queries.answer: No, this is a PPO plan so you do not need a referral to see a specialist. You can see any specialist directly.

common_queries.query: How much does a primary care visit cost?
common_queries.answer: In-network primary care visits cost between $0 to $10 copay. Out-of-network visits cost 30% coinsurance.
Yes, preferred generic drugs (Tier 1) have $0 copay for both 30-day retail and 90-day mail order. Non-preferred generics (Tier 2) cost $10 for 30-day retail and $25 for 90-day mail order.
Yes, preventive care is covered at 100% in-network with no deductible, copay, or coinsurance. This includes annual physicals, mammograms, vaccines, and screenings.

common_queries.query: Does the plan cover vision and dental?
common_queries.answer: Yes, the plan includes vision benefits ($0 eye exam, $200/year for glasses/contacts) and dental benefits ($0 for cleanings/exams, 30% coinsurance for fillings, major procedures not covered).

Services requiring prior authorization include: MRI/CT/PET scans, inpatient hospital admissions, outpatient surgeries over $2,000, home health care, DME over $500, all specialty prescriptions, and skilled nursing facility admissions.

common_queries.query: How much does an emergency room visit cost?
common_queries.answer: Emergency room visits have a $120 copay, which is the same for both in-network and out-of-network. The copay is waived if you are admitted to the hospital.
Yes, in-network telehealth visits are $0 copay for primary care and $20 copay for specialists. Out-of-network telehealth is not covered.

common_queries.query: What is covered under mental health?
common_queries.answer: Outpatient mental health therapy is $20 copay in-network, psychiatrist visits are $35 copay in-network. Inpatient mental health is $295/day for days 1-5, then $0 for days 6+.
Yes, routine hearing exams are $0 copay. Hearing aids are available through the Humana TruHearing program for $699 to $999 per device.
SilverSneakers is a fitness program included at no extra cost with this plan, providing access to fitness centers and exercise classes.

common_queries.query: How much does a specialist visit cost?
common_queries.answer: Specialist visits cost $35 copay in-network and 40% coinsurance out-of-network. No referral is required.

common_queries.query: What happens if I go out of network?
common_queries.answer: You can see out-of-network providers, but you'll pay higher costs. Out-of-network services have higher deductible ($850), higher coinsurance (typically 30-50%), and count toward a combined $8,000 out-of-pocket maximum.

glossary.definition: A type of health plan that offers flexibility to see any provider, with lower costs when using in-network providers and no referral requirements for specialists.
The amount you pay for covered healthcare services before your insurance plan starts to pay.
The most you pay for covered services in a year. Once you reach this amount, your insurance pays 100% of covered services.
A fixed amount you pay for a covered healthcare service, such as $35 for a specialist visit.
Your share of the costs of a covered healthcare service, calculated as a percentage (for example, 30%) of the allowed amount for the service.
Healthcare providers that have a contract with your health insurance plan. Using in-network providers costs less.
Healthcare providers that do not have a contract with your health insurance plan. Using out-of-network providers costs more.
A type of Medicare health plan offered by private companies that contract with Medicare to provide Part A and Part B benefits, often including additional benefits like prescription drug coverage.
Approval from your health insurance plan required before receiving certain services or medications to ensure they are covered.
A list of prescription drugs covered by your health insurance plan, organized into tiers with different cost-sharing amounts.
High-cost prescription medications used to treat complex or rare conditions, requiring special handling and often filled through specialty pharmacies.
Healthcare services focused on preventing illness, such as annual checkups, screenings, and vaccinations, often covered at 100% with no cost-sharing.
Healthcare services delivered remotely through video or phone appointments with healthcare providers.
Medical equipment ordered by a doctor for use in the home, such as wheelchairs, walkers, hospital beds, or oxygen equipment.
A facility that provides skilled nursing care and rehabilitation services for patients who need professional nursing care but not hospital-level care.
